data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 ranks the torn-tail repair gap as 'lowest blast radius among the guard-death gaps' (Priority 5) because partial coverage allegedly already exists. But PARKED.md explicitly classifies the torn-tail repair as a guard whose death NO test detects. If a test in the ring already exercises the gate-level repair, then by PARKED.md's own definition this is not a guard-death gap at all — it is a closed gap. SRC_002 cannot simultaneously assert the guard's death is undetected AND that partial coverage already exists; the 'partial coverage' framing is invented to justify a low priority, but a guard whose death passes the suite has ZERO detection, not partial detection. A torn-tail in a ring buffer corrupts a data-integrity record, which by the problem's own blast-radius hierarchy (append-only corruption vs. hiding a refusal) must rank above mere security-refusal hiding, not below it.
